items.title: Armand Hug Interview, 1976-02-13
items.q: It brings to mind right there a very funny story about Chink Morton, the old bass player. ... He played, he played with, with the Red Dead Kings for a while.

ctx.x: And then you went and played in the French Quarter for a while, I guess.

I went to work at a cabaret. It was called the Cabarets in those days. It was called the Valencia Cabaret. It was where the Royal Sinesta Hotel is today, on Bourbon Street. And I worked with various little groups, three-piece groups there, from time to time. Some of the musicians I played with there was Chink Morton's son, Chink Morton Jr. Eddie Miller played there with me for a while. Who's now playing with Pete Fountain. Yes. And Eddie played alto sax in those days. He wasn't playing tenor. And Al Hesman, banjo…

items.title: Armand Hug Interview, 1960-07-14
items.q: being associated with fellows like Chink Morton, old timers like that. They really helped to a great extent.

ctx.x: Kind of like a Wausau just played for fun. They just go around and listen and pick up things. That's right.

I would say my association with Buzzy Williams was really great. And then playing around the spots, being associated with fellows like Chink Morton, old timers like that. They really helped to a great extent. Harry Shields. I met Leon Rapolo one time when I was at the Valencia. And he sat in and played. But he just played a few tunes and that was all.
Was he playing good then? He was playing real good then.
